title: Virtual reality as support before elective tumor surgery to improve anxious/depressive symptoms
summary: A major operation is often associated with stress, fear, and uncertainty – not only because of the procedure itself but also due to the anesthesia. Patients with cancer are often additionally burdened, as they may already have undergone stressful treatments such as chemotherapy. Virtual reality (VR) can help in this situation: with special headsets, patients are immersed in a calming, positive environment that provides distraction and relief. First studies show that VR can reduce pain and anxiety during chemotherapy. However, it has not yet been investigated whether VR can also improve well-being and positively influence surgical outcomes before major cancer operations. The aim of this study is therefore to evaluate the use of VR headsets for reducing stress and anxiety prior to major abdominal surgery in patients with gastrointestinal tumors.
conditions: Malignant neoplasm of anus and anal canal
Malignant neoplasm of liver and intrahepatic bile ducts
Malignant neoplasm of other and unspecified parts of biliary tract

interventions.name: Use of the VR headset on the evening before surgery, elective surgery on the following day
No use of the VR headset on the evening before surgery, elective surgery on the following day (control group)

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- Patients ≥18 years of age capable of giving informed consent
- Signed written informed consent
- Oncological disease
- Mental and physical condition adequate to participate in study procedures as assessed by the investigator
- Indication for surgery for tumor resection
Exclusion criteria:
- Contraindications to the use of a VR headset as assessed by the investigator, e.g., known seizure disorder, uncontrolled cerebral metastases
- Participation in another interventional clinical trial
